text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: serving-runtime pool us-west1 reported repeated cudaIllegalMemoryAccess on node gpu-uw1-07. Triggered by high-concurrency generation requests. Pager: <https://pager.example/INC12345>

olivia: seeing container restarts on 3 pods in the pool, OOMs + illegal memory access logs. Noticed spike in paging/eviction around 14:02 UTC.

maria: logs (excerpt) ->
```
2026-03-15T14:01:58Z runtime: tokengen failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress: device-side assert or invalid device address
E runtime: worker[12] crashed: container restart
```

olivia: dmesg from gpu-uw1-07 attached ->
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x86)
[ 12345.679002] kernel: nvidia: invalid device address 0x7ffdeabc1234 (misaligned)
[ 12345.679103] kernel: nnodes: pagewalk error, SMMU: deviceaddr=0x7ffdeabc1234
```

kern_eng: this looks like the familiar misaligned-deviceaddr pagewalk that we've seen when KV-cache growth crosses a page boundary under concurrent eviction. Possible kernel/NVIDIA driver edge-case.

raj: customer impact status? which tenants saw 5xxs?

maria: routing shows ~12 customers had >1% error rate in the last 5m; top ones are low-latency trading-prod and search-bench. Latency for others spiked 200-400ms due to retries.

olivia: mitigation proposal:
- cordon + drain gpu-uw1-07
- rollback runtime lib to previous dev-build that had conservative KV allocation
- set routing rule to fallback to cpu-quantized model for affected routes
- reduce max batch size to 1 on the pool
- collect full nv-hostengine + kernel logs and upload to S3

sre_bot: commenters: cordon command queued: `kubectl cordon gpu-uw1-07` -> OK

deploy-bot: drain in progress: `kubectl drain gpu-uw1-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (pods being rescheduled)

maria: started route override -> fallback to cpu-quantized for trading-prod and search-bench (instant error drop observed)

olivia: reducing batch size and disabling prefetch on pool config now. Patch applied via console.

kern_eng: please grab `dmesg`, `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`, and the GPU coredump from /var/crash. I'm going to repro locally with concurrent eviction. If I can reproduce, we'll escalate to driver vendor.

maria: uploaded logs -> s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC12345/gpu-uw1-07/

raj: any indication this is due to the recent kernel live-patch we rolled last week?

kern_eng: initial look: timestamps correlate with live-patch rollouts but stacktrace points to race in pagewalk handling in our runtime when KV-cache invalidation races with async prefetch. Need a repro.

olivia: after drain, node shows healthy per node-exporter, no more illegal_address messages for 5m. But two pods restarted with exit code 137 before being drained (OOM). We're adding node-level memory headroom next run.

sre_bot: rollback to previous runtime image initiated: `image: redwood/runtime:v2026-03-11-rc3` -> in progress

deploy-bot: runtime rollback completed on the pool. Observed drop in illegal memory errors on remaining nodes.

maria: customer comms: drafted short blurb for affected customers, including ETA for root cause. Will mark as degraded with no data loss.

olivia: follow-ups:
- kern_eng to try to reproduce and file vendor bug if needed
- eng-runtime to add guard against misaligned deviceaddr writes (bounds checks on KV eviction)
- infra to add node-level OOM margin and lower batch default for GPU pools when KV-cache enabled

kern_eng: repro steps added to ISSUE-9876, attaching minimal repro harness and dmesg. If vendor asks, we'll provide coredump and repro.

raj: assigning SEV owner: olivia (primary), kern_eng (secondary). SEV doc: <https://incidents/redwood/INC12345>

olivia: handing on-call to raj for overnight monitoring. Summary: detected cuda illegal memory access tied to misaligned device address/pagewalk race during high-concurrency KV-cache eviction. We cordoned/drained one noisy node, rolled runtime back, applied routing fallback, reduced batch size. Customers served via fallback with degraded latency. Next: repro and vendor escalation.

raj: acked. I'll follow overnight and post a final incident update in ~2h. Please ping me if you get a driver vendor contact.

oncall-bot: NOTE: thread updated with SEV status -> OPEN, priority P1, owner olivia. Logs: s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC12345/

olivia: logs and playbook attached. Leaving monitoring alerts live. :white_check_mark:
